PROLOGUE

"FATHER, … this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent."

"God our Saviour desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth."

"There is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved" - than the name of JESUS.

I. The life of man - to know and love God

God, infinitely perfect and blessed in himself, in a plan of sheer goodness freely created man to make him share in his own blessed life. For this reason, at every time and in every place, God draws close to man. He calls man to seek him, to know him, to love him with all his strength. He calls together all men, scattered and divided by sin, into the unity of his family, the Church. To accomplish this, when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son as Redeemer and Saviour. In his Son and through him, he invites men to become, in the Holy Spirit, his adopted children and thus heirs of his blessed life.

So that this call should resound throughout the world, Christ sent forth the apostles he had chosen, commissioning them to proclaim the gospel: "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, to the close of the age." Strengthened by this mission, the apostles "went forth and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the message by the signs that attended it."

Those who with God's help have welcomed Christ's call and freely responded to it are urged on by love of Christ to proclaim the Good News everywhere in the world. This treasure, received from the apostles, has been faithfully guarded by their successors. All Christ's faithful are called to hand it on from generation to generation, by professing the faith, by living it in fraternal sharing, and by celebrating it in liturgy and prayer.

facets.text: The Catechism opens by defining eternal life and the very purpose of human existence as knowing and loving God. Because God is infinitely perfect and blessed in himself, his act of creating man springs not from need but from a plan of sheer goodness, freely willing that man share in his own blessed life. Human happiness and destiny are therefore ordered entirely toward communion with God.
facets.question: What is the ultimate purpose of human life?

facets.text: God is not distant but perpetually initiates relationship, drawing close to man at every time and in every place and calling him to seek, know, and love him with all his strength. This universal divine initiative precedes and enables any human response, showing that the desire for God is answered by God's own prior movement toward humanity. The call is addressed to all people without exception.
facets.question: Does God take the first step in reaching out to humanity?

facets.text: Sin scatters and divides humanity, but God's saving plan gathers all people into the unity of his family, the Church. The Church is thus understood as the divinely willed communion that overcomes the fragmentation caused by sin, reuniting what had been separated into one family of God. Salvation has an inherently communal and ecclesial character, not merely an individual one.
facets.question: Why does God gather people into the Church rather than saving them individually?

facets.text: In the fullness of time God sent his Son as Redeemer and Saviour, and there is no other name under heaven by which men must be saved than the name of Jesus. Through the Son and in the Holy Spirit, God invites men to become his adopted children and heirs of his blessed life. This adoption in Christ is the concrete means by which humanity is drawn into the Trinitarian life.
facets.question: How do human beings become adopted children and heirs of God?

facets.text: Christ commissioned the apostles he had chosen to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching them, with the promise of his abiding presence to the close of the age. The Great Commission establishes the missionary mandate of the Church and grounds its authority to proclaim, baptize, and teach in Christ's own sending. The Lord himself works with the apostles, confirming their preaching by accompanying signs.
facets.question: What is the origin of the Church's mission to evangelize all nations?

facets.text: Those who welcome and freely respond to Christ's call are impelled by love of Christ to proclaim the Good News everywhere. The faith received is therefore not a private possession to be kept but a treasure meant to be shared, and love is the interior force that drives evangelization. Free human response cooperates with God's grace in spreading the gospel.
facets.question: What moves believers to share the gospel with others?

facets.text: The deposit of faith received from the apostles has been faithfully guarded by their successors and is handed on from generation to generation. This transmission occurs through three interrelated acts: professing the faith, living it in fraternal sharing, and celebrating it in liturgy and prayer. The lived faith of the Church thus integrates creed, charity, and worship as a single inheritance passed forward.
facets.question: How is the faith of the apostles preserved and handed on through the generations?

merged.annotation:
SUMMARY: The Prologue of the Catechism sets forth the purpose of human life as knowing and loving God, the divine initiative of salvation in Christ, the gathering of humanity into the Church, and the apostolic mission to transmit the faith. Its scope is foundational and doctrinal, framing the entire catechetical project.

[DOCTRINAL | explicit]: Man's purpose and eternal life consist in knowing and loving God, whose creation of man flows from sheer goodness to share his blessed life.
[DOCTRINAL | traditional]: God perpetually takes the initiative, drawing near to all people everywhere and calling them to seek, know, and love him before any human response.
[DOCTRINAL | traditional]: Sin scatters humanity, but God's plan reunites all into the one family of the Church, giving salvation a communal and ecclesial character.
[DOCTRINAL | explicit]: God sent his Son as sole Redeemer, and through Christ in the Spirit humanity becomes adopted children and heirs of divine life.
[SCRIPTURAL | explicit]: Christ's Great Commission to make disciples, baptize, and teach all nations, with his promise to remain always, grounds the Church's missionary mandate.
[MORAL | inferential]: Love of Christ impels those who freely respond to his call to proclaim the gospel, making faith a treasure to be shared rather than kept.
[DOCTRINAL | explicit]: The apostolic deposit of faith is guarded by successors and transmitted through professing, living in fraternal sharing, and celebrating the faith in liturgy and prayer.
